title: Shadow Traffic: Quality Deltas Dashboards — mockups + query snippets (cardinality-safe)
body:
Slide 1 — Context / goals
- We need a single dashboard surface for “quality deltas” between control and shadow variants, tied to a Shadow Experiment (and optionally a Rollout).
- Must be safe by default: bounded cardinality, predictable query cost, and usable for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Must answer:
  1) Is candidate quality better/worse than control?
  2) Is the measurement reliable (coverage, CI width, scoring lag)?
  3) Where is the regression (segments: route family, request type, tenant tier, region)?

---

Slide 2 — Event/metric naming assumptions (v1)
We’re aligning to quality-metrics-observability-standard.

Core timeseries (aggregates emitted by pipeline; do NOT compute from raw events in dashboard):
- shadow_quality_score_sum{metric_name, experiment_id, variant="control|shadow", route_family, request_type, region, tenant_tier}
- shadow_quality_score_count{same dims}
- shadow_quality_bad_count{metric_name, experiment_id, variant, ...}  # for binary pass/fail
- shadow_shadow_requests_total{experiment_id, ...}
- shadow_control_requests_total{experiment_id, ...}
- shadow_scored_pairs_total{experiment_id, ...}
- shadow_scoring_lag_seconds_p50/p95{experiment_id, pipeline="scoring"}
- shadow_pipeline_dropped_pairs_total{reason, experiment_id}
- shadow_target_error_rate{experiment_id, shadow_target_id, http_status_class}

Important: experiment_id is required; route is bucketed into route_family.

---

Slide 3 — Dashboard 1: “Shadow Experiment Overview” (top-level)
Layout mock (single page):

[Header]
- Experiment: <name> (<experiment_id>)   Status: Running/Stopped   Started: <ts>   Owner: <user>
- Control: <model/version/profile>   Shadow: <model/version/profile>
- Sampling: X% shadowed   Fingerprint: stable_hash_v1
- Time range selector: [Last 1h | 6h | 24h | Custom]

[Row A — Health / coverage]
(1) Coverage gauge: scored_pairs / shadow_pairs
(2) Scoring lag: p50/p95 tiles
(3) Drop rate by reason (small bar)
(4) Shadow target errors (stacked by 4xx/5xx/timeout)

[Row B — Quality delta headline]
- “Primary metric delta” (default: instruction_following_score or format_adherence)
  Chart: delta over time with confidence band
  - delta = mean(shadow) - mean(control)
  - show CI (Wilson for binary; bootstrap or normal approx for continuous)

[Row C — Score breakdown (top N metrics)]
- Table:
  metric_name | control_mean | shadow_mean | delta | CI_low | CI_high | n_control | n_shadow | regressed?

[Row D — Segment explorer]
- Controls:
  - segment dimension dropdown (route_family / request_type / region / tenant_tier)
  - top-K selector (K=10 default)
  - “Only regressions” toggle
- Output:
  - bar chart of delta by segment with CI whiskers
  - click a segment → deep link to “Segment drilldown” dashboard

---

Slide 4 — Dashboard 2: “Quality Delta (Drilldown)”
Purpose: investigate one metric + one segmentation.

Mock:
[Filters]
- experiment_id (required)
- metric_name (required)
- route_family (optional)
- request_type (optional)
- region (optional)
- tenant_tier (optional)
- model_role: control/shadow (optional; default both)

[Panels]
1) Timeseries: control_mean vs shadow_mean (two lines)
2) Timeseries: delta with CI band
3) Distribution proxy:
   - if we have histograms: overlay of score histogram buckets
   - if not: show quantiles p50/p90 per variant (from pipeline)
4) “Scoring integrity” row:
   - scored_pairs rate
   - lag p95
   - dropped_pairs by reason

Notes:
- Avoid free-text labels. All filters must be from enumerated sets.
- Default to 6h window for ‘running experiments’ to reduce noise.

---

Slide 5 — Dashboard 3: “Time-window comparison (before/after)”
Ask: did quality change after rollout/config change or after we updated shadow target?

Mock:
[Controls]
- Window A: start/end
- Window B: start/end
- Compare mode: delta-of-deltas

[Panels]
- Table: metric_name | delta_A | delta_B | (delta_B - delta_A) | CI | n
- Sparkline row per metric: delta over full timeline with window markers

Rules:
- Must show sample sizes per window.
- When CI is wide (or n < min_n), display “insufficient power” badge.

---

Slide 6 — Grafana/PromQL-like query snippets (timeseries)
Assuming metrics are emitted as sums/counts; compute mean:

(1) Mean score by variant
mean_score = sum(rate(shadow_quality_score_sum{experiment_id="$exp", metric_name="$metric", variant=~"control|shadow", route_family=~"$route_family", request_type=~"$request_type", region=~"$region", tenant_tier=~"$tenant_tier"}[5m]))
           / sum(rate(shadow_quality_score_count{same labels}[5m]))

(2) Delta mean (shadow - control)
mean_shadow = (sum(rate(...{variant="shadow"}[5m])) / sum(rate(..._count{variant="shadow"}[5m])))
mean_control = (sum(rate(...{variant="control"}[5m])) / sum(rate(..._count{variant="control"}[5m])))
delta = mean_shadow - mean_control

(3) Coverage
coverage = sum(rate(shadow_scored_pairs_total{experiment_id="$exp"}[5m]))
         / sum(rate(shadow_shadow_requests_total{experiment_id="$exp"}[5m]))

(4) Scoring lag tiles
p50 = avg_over_time(shadow_scoring_lag_seconds_p50{experiment_id="$exp"}[10m])
p95 = avg_over_time(shadow_scoring_lag_seconds_p95{experiment_id="$exp"}[10m])

Notes:
- We should prefer rate() over raw counters.
- Use [5m] for charts; [1m] makes dashboards noisy and expensive.

---

Slide 7 — Binary metric delta (pass/fail) + Wilson CI (pipeline responsibility)
For pass/fail metrics (e.g., format_ok, refusal_ok), the dashboard should NOT attempt CI math.

Instead pipeline publishes precomputed aggregates per interval:
- shadow_quality_pass_rate{...}
- shadow_quality_pass_rate_ci_low{...}
- shadow_quality_pass_rate_ci_high{...}

Then delta band is computed as:
- delta = pass_rate_shadow - pass_rate_control
- CI for delta: conservative combine (low_shadow - high_control, high_shadow - low_control)

Why:
- Doing Wilson or Newcombe interval math in Grafana is brittle.
- Keeps dashboards consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

---

Slide 8 — Segment explorer: cardinality-safe breakdown patterns
Allowed segment dims (v1):
- route_family (bucketed; max ~200 per org, but dashboard shows Top-K)
- request_type (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)
- region
- tenant_tier (hosted/free/pro/enterprise or dedicated/private)

Explicitly NOT allowed:
- prompt_id, request_id, user_id, customer_id, raw model_id string if it’s unbounded (use Redwood-internal model_key)
- arbitrary headers

Top-K implementation:
- Use recorded rules or pre-aggregation to compute top-K route_family by traffic volume per experiment in the selected time window.
- Panel query should join only to that top-K list (or apply a dashboard variable that is pre-populated).

Fallback when cardinality exceeds limit:
- Show banner: “Too many segments. Narrow filters or switch to route_family_group.”

---

Slide 9 — Example table panel query (top metrics)
Goal: top metrics table with delta and CI. Approach:
- Pipeline writes a small ‘metric_summary’ table keyed by (experiment_id, metric_name, time_bucket, segment dims) with:
  control_mean, shadow_mean, delta_mean, ci_low, ci_high, n

Dashboard reads with a single query (pseudo-SQL):
SELECT metric_name,
       avg(control_mean) AS control_mean,
       avg(shadow_mean) AS shadow_mean,
       avg(delta_mean)  AS delta,
       min(ci_low)      AS ci_low,
       max(ci_high)     AS ci_high,
       sum(n_control)   AS n_control,
       sum(n_shadow)    AS n_shadow
FROM shadow_quality_metric_summary
WHERE experiment_id = $exp
  AND time_bucket BETWEEN $start AND $end
  AND route_family IN ($route_family)   -- optional
  AND request_type IN ($request_type)   -- optional
GROUP BY metric_name
ORDER BY abs(delta) DESC
LIMIT 12;

Note: This avoids multi-metric PromQL hacks and keeps it fast.

---

Slide 10 — Visual conventions (to match rollouts UI)
Color + badges:
- Delta > 0 and CI excludes 0 → green “Improvement”
- Delta < 0 and CI excludes 0 → red “Regression”
- CI includes 0 or n < min_n → gray “Inconclusive”

Min_n defaults (proposal; from Sana/Selene notes):
- Binary metrics: min_n_per_variant = 500 (for stable +/- 1–2% signals)
- Continuous rubric scores: min_n_per_variant = 200 (but require CI width threshold)

Add “CI width” warning:
- If (ci_high - ci_low) > threshold, add ‘wide CI’ label.

---

Slide 11 — Review comments / open questions (captured during Observability + SRE review)
1) (Sean G.) “Make coverage and scoring lag the first thing you see. Otherwise people trust deltas that are based on 3 samples.”
   Action: Row A health tiles pinned at top; add ‘data quality’ banner when lag p95 > 10m OR coverage < 0.7.

2) (Nadia R.) “We should not query raw shadow pair events from Grafana at all; summary tables only.”
   Action: make summary-table dependency explicit; dashboards block if summary table missing.

3) (Caleb J.) “Route dimension needs to be route_family, not route_id; also enforce Top-K.”
   Action: dashboard variable route_family is populated by a precomputed top list; no free-text.

4) (Selene H.) “Delta on continuous scores can be misleading if variance changes. We should at least show quantiles.”
   Action: add quantile panels per variant if available from scoring pipeline.

5) (PM feedback via Marissa) “Default view should be ‘one number’ and ‘is it worse?’—don’t overwhelm.”
   Action: headline metric + simple summary table; advanced panels collapsed by default.

Open questions:
- What’s the default primary metric for v1? (instruction_following vs format_adherence vs safety_refusal)
- Do we publish CI bands per metric type from pipeline or do some in dashboard?
- How do we represent rubric version changes in the dashboard header (rubric_version pinned per experiment)?

---

Slide 12 — Next steps / TODO
- [Allison] finalize dashboard JSON + variables once metric summary table schema is locked (see ENG-5404).
- [Nadia] confirm retention + downsampling granularity (5m vs 15m buckets) for Dedicated.
- [Sean] define alert thresholds aligned with dashboard banners (lag/coverage/error).
- [Selene/Sana] provide recommended min_n + CI method per metric type for v1.

Appendix — Notes to self
- Keep a “Debug” dashboard hidden behind feature flag for oncall: drop reasons, queue depth, worker error codes.
- Ensure all dashboards render in Private with no external calls; avoid links that assume SaaS Grafana.
